bull.t: Strategic customer agreements improve demand visibility
bull.b: Long-term customer agreements can improve demand visibility, support capacity planning and deepen relationships with major buyers. Their broadening coverage may reduce reliance on purely spot-market volumes, although some pricing remains variable.

bull.t: HBM and advanced memory technology leadership
bull.b: Successful HBM, DRAM and NAND technology ramps strengthen Micron’s position in AI infrastructure and other compute-intensive markets. Faster yields and advanced packaging can support differentiated products and durable customer qualification.

bull.t: Strong balance sheet and cash generation
bull.b: High cash generation and low leverage provide financial flexibility to fund capacity expansion, technology development and shareholder returns. A stronger capital structure also gives Micron greater resilience when memory conditions weaken.

bear.b: Micron’s dependence on DRAM and NAND supply-demand cycles creates material volatility in pricing, margins and cash flow. Even strong execution cannot fully remove the risk that future oversupply causes a sharp earnings reset.

Large fab, packaging and technology investments are necessary to capture AI-related demand but increase fixed costs and execution risk. Higher operating expenses could pressure free cash flow and margins if ramps or demand take longer.

bear.t: Supply constraints and pricing economics remain uncertain
bear.b: Long lead times, skilled-worker shortages and infrastructure limits constrain supply expansion, while rising manufacturing complexity increases costs. Variable SCA pricing and higher cost per bit could reduce the durability of current margins.
